issues.title: WebServer class missing final keyword
issues.description: The WebServer class is not designed for subclassing (it implements a singleton pattern with sharedInstance) but lacks the 'final' keyword, allowing unintended inheritance and missing compiler optimization opportunities
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

issues.title: Thread safety violation calling @MainActor completion handler from background thread
issues.description: In the handleServerTrust method, when SSL/TLS certificate validation fails (guard else clause), the @MainActor-isolated completionHandler is called directly from the background dispatchQueue without using ensureMainThread wrapper. This violates Swift Concurrency's actor isolation and can cause runtime crashes or data races. The success path correctly wraps the completion call in ensureMainThread, but the failure path at line 1343 does not, creating inconsistent thread safety behavior.

issues.title: ensureMainThread generic function loses return value when dispatched asynchronously
issues.description: The generic ensureMainThread<T> function was modified to return T? but has a critical flaw: when not on the main thread, it dispatches the work asynchronously to main queue and immediately returns nil, discarding the actual computation result. This breaks any caller that depends on the return value, as they will always receive nil when called from background threads. The function's contract promises to return the work result but fails to do so in the async dispatch path.

issues.title: MainThreadThrottler timing logic inverted causing throttling to never execute
issues.description: In the throttle method, lastExecutionTime is updated to Date() BEFORE checking the threshold guard condition. This means timeIntervalSinceNow will always be approximately 0 (since it was just set), which will never be less than -threshold (a negative value). The guard condition will always fail, preventing the completion from ever executing. This completely breaks the throttling mechanism, causing any code depending on throttled callbacks to never receive them.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31547 - Refactor FXIOS-13122 [Swift 6] Remove @Sendable from closures marked as @MainActor

structured_output.summary:
This PR says it's a mechanical Swift 6 cleanup: it removes the redundant `@Sendable` from about 40 closure types that are already `@MainActor`. Under SE-0434, global-actor-isolated function types are implicitly Sendable, so most of these edits are safe and make the signatures easier to read.

Several of the changed files also contain behavior changes that the description doesn't mention. Two of them are real regressions:
- **`MainThreadThrottler.throttle`:** the `lastExecutionTime` assignment now runs before the guard, so the completion never fires when the threshold is above zero.
- **`handleServerTrust`:** the `ensureMainThread` wrapper was removed from the default-handling path, so a `@MainActor` WebKit completion handler is now called synchronously on `DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated)`.

There are also smaller unrelated edits:
- The generic `ensureMainThread<T>` now returns `T?`.
- `final` was dropped from `WebServer`.
- A stray double space was added in `RelayController`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The annotation cleanup is fine, but two changes the PR doesn't mention break things. The throttler change stops homepage impressions, story feed scroll handling and tab coordinator work from running, and fails existing unit tests. The server-trust change calls a main-actor WebKit callback from a background queue. Both need to be reverted before merge.

architecture.overview:
The app uses `@MainActor` closure types throughout: WebKit delegate callbacks, Redux reducers, menu and action-sheet tap handlers, and helpers like `ensureMainThread` and `MainThreadThrottler` that move work onto the main thread. Before this PR those types were written `@MainActor @Sendable`. Swift 6 (SE-0434) already treats global-actor-isolated function types as Sendable, so the PR removes the redundant attribute from protocols, typealiases, struct fields and their conforming mocks.

Alongside the annotation changes, the PR changes behavior in a few helpers. It changes the return type of the generic `ensureMainThread<T>` in `DispatchQueueHelper.swift` and reorders the guard in `MainThreadThrottler.throttle`. It removes the `ensureMainThread` hop in `BrowserViewController.handleServerTrust`, which runs on `userInitiatedQueue` (a global queue). It also drops `final` from `WebServer`.
steps: Start at `BrowserKit/Sources/Common/Utilities/DispatchQueueHelper.swift` and `DispatchQueueInterface.swift`: these are the main-thread hop helpers. The non-generic signature only loses `@Sendable`. The generic overload now returns `T?`.

Look at the shared types whose signatures changed: `Reducer` (Redux), `MenuElement.action`, `SingleActionViewModel` handlers, `RelayPopulateCompletion`, `SearchEngineCompletion`. These are pure annotation removals.

Review the WebKit delegate conformances in `BrowserViewController+WebViewDelegates.swift`, `BrowserWebUIDelegate.swift` and `FxAWebViewController.swift`. These signatures now match the SDK's `@MainActor` completion handler types.
Check `handleServerTrust` (BrowserViewController+WebViewDelegates.swift ~1329-1351). Its work runs on `userInitiatedQueue`, and the PR removed the main-thread hop on one of its two exit paths.
Check `MainThreadThrottler.throttle` (Client/Utils/MainThreadThrottler.swift). Callers in HomepageViewController, StoriesFeedViewController and WindowSimpleTabsCoordinator depend on this guard order.
Finally, the protocol mocks under the test targets (MockThrottler, MockAppAuthenticator, MockTabQueue, etc.) were updated to match the new protocol signatures.

findings.title: Reordered guard in MainThreadThrottler means completion never runs
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Utils/MainThreadThrottler.swift`, `throttle(completion:)` (lines 26-30) now assigns `lastExecutionTime = Date()` before the guard. As a result the guard always fails for positive thresholds and the completion never runs. Restore the original order: check the guard first, then set `lastExecutionTime = Date()`, then `DispatchQueue.main.async(execute: completion)`. Keep the new `@MainActor` closure signature without `@Sendable`. Run `MainThreadThrottlerTests` to confirm all three tests pass.

findings.title: handleServerTrust calls @MainActor completionHandler from a background queue
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/BrowserViewController/Extensions/BrowserViewController+WebViewDelegates.swift`, `handleServerTrust` (around lines 1329-1351) runs on `userInitiatedQueue`, a global background queue. The PR removed the `ensureMainThread { ... }` wrapper around `completionHandler(.performDefaultHandling, nil)` in the guard's else branch, so a `@MainActor` WebKit completion handler is now called off the main thread. Restore the `ensureMainThread` wrapper so this path matches the `.useCredential` path below it. Only drop `@Sendable` from the signature.

findings.title: Generic ensureMainThread<T> now returns a misleading T?
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Sources/Common/Utilities/DispatchQueueHelper.swift` lines 22-33, the generic `ensureMainThread<T>` was changed to return `T?`: the value when on main, `nil` when deferred. This is outside the scope of the @Sendable cleanup, its semantics are ambiguous, and nothing uses the return value. Restore the original `Void`-returning body (`_ = work()` in both branches) and keep only the `@Sendable` removal from the parameter type.

findings.title: `final` removed from WebServer without explanation
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Application/WebServer.swift` line 18, `final` was removed from `class WebServer: WebServerProtocol, @unchecked Sendable`. Nothing subclasses it, and because the conformance is `@unchecked Sendable`, a subclass could add unsynchronized state. Put `final` back. The only intended change in this file is dropping `@Sendable` from the `handler` parameter of `registerMainBundleResource`.

findings.title: Stray double space in RelayPopulateCompletion typealias
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/RelayController.swift` line 10, remove the extra space between `@MainActor` and `(RelayMaskGenerationResult)` in the `RelayPopulateCompletion` typealias.

findings.title: The bulk @Sendable removal itself is sound
findings.body: With Swift 6 / SE-0434, global-actor-isolated function types such as `@MainActor () -> Void` are implicitly `Sendable`. Removing `@Sendable` is therefore safe even where the closure is stored in a `Sendable` struct (`MenuElement`, `SingleActionViewModel`) or passed to `DispatchQueue.main.async`. The protocol changes (`AppAuthenticationProtocol`, `TabQueue`, `MainThreadThrottlerProtocol`, `TabProviderProtocol`, `WKEngineWebView`) were applied consistently to their mocks, so the test targets should still type-check. The PR would be easier to review if the behavior changes flagged above were dropped and it stayed purely mechanical.
